question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The manager tried to placate the angry customers by offering them a full refund.

solution_text.en:
Meaning: placate = to make someone less angry; to calm or soothe (शांत करना, मनाना)

Why the others are wrong.

• Pacify = to calm someone who is angry or upset (शांत करना). Same meaning → correct.

• Provoke = to make someone angry on purpose (भड़काना): opposite meaning — the trap.

• Implicate = to show that someone is involved in a crime or fault (फँसाना, लिप्त दिखाना): look-alike of placate / implicate, unrelated meaning.

• Flatter = to please someone with praise that is more than they deserve (चापलूसी करना): same field (pleasing someone), but it means praising, not calming anger. A refund calms anger; it does not praise anyone.

Word help. refund (धनवापसी)

Placate and pacify both start with 'p' and both bring peace: placate = pacify.

question.en:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who pretends to be ill in order to escape duty or work

solution_text.en:
Meaning: Malingerer = a person who pretends to be ill, or exaggerates an illness, to avoid duty or work (बीमारी का बहाना करके काम से बचने वाला, कामचोर)

The verb is malinger (बीमारी का बहाना बनाना).

Why the others are wrong.

• Hypochondriac = a person who genuinely believes he is ill and worries too much about health (वहमी रोगी). He is not pretending, so he is not dodging work on purpose.

• Truant = a student who stays away from school without permission (स्कूल से भागने वाला). No pretence of illness is involved.

• Sluggard = a habitually lazy, slow person (आलसी, सुस्त). Lazy, but the definition needs the pretence of illness.

Word help.

• pretend (दिखावा करना, बहाना करना)

• escape duty (कर्तव्य से बचना)

Two clues lock it: 'pretends to be ill' + 'to escape duty'. Imagined illness = hypochondriac; faked illness = malingerer.

solution_text.en:
Opener test.

Q introduces the people, the problem (falling groundwater) and the plan (reviving the ponds). It needs nothing before it, so Q opens.

Links.

• Q → R: "They" in R refers to the people of the hamlet in Q, and R lists the work they did to revive the ponds.

• R → P: P gives the result of that work: within two monsoons the wells held water.

• P → S: "That success" in S points back to the result in P, and S closes with what followed.

Order: Q R P S → the third sentence is P.

The paragraph.

Faced with falling groundwater, the people of a small hamlet in Rajasthan decided to revive their old stepped ponds. They cleared the silt, repaired the stone embankments and dug channels to guide the run-off from the hills. Within two monsoons, the wells that had run dry every May began to hold water through the summer. That success has since persuaded three neighbouring villages to try the same approach.

Problem → action → result → spread: the natural order of any 'success story' paragraph.

Word help: silt (गाद), embankment (तटबंध), run-off (बहकर आने वाला वर्षा जल)

question.en:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The minister was criticised for hosting a lavish wedding while the district was reeling under drought.

solution_text.en:
Meaning: lavish = rich, costly and more than enough; spending money freely (भव्य, फ़िज़ूलखर्ची वाला)

Opposite → frugal = simple and economical; spending little (मितव्ययी, किफ़ायती)

Why the others are wrong.

• Opulent = rich, costly and luxurious (वैभवशाली, ठाठदार): same meaning as lavish — the synonym trap.

• Grudging = given unwillingly (अनिच्छा से दिया गया): opposes the other sense of lavish (generous, as in lavish praise). A wedding cannot be 'grudging'; the sentence is about costly display.

• Livid = furiously angry (आगबबूला): look-alike of lavish, unrelated meaning.

Word help. reeling under (बुरी तरह जूझ रहा)

Lavish spends freely; frugal spends carefully: think of a lavish feast versus a frugal meal.

option_1.en: The groundsmen covered the pitch with sheets before the rain began.

option_2.en: The singer could not reach the high pitch of the final note.

option_3.en: The scouts helped us pitch our tents near the river.

option_4.en: She made a confident pitch to the investors.

question.en: Select the sentence in which the word 'pitch' refers to how high or low a sound is.

solution_text.en:
Meaning asked: pitch = the highness or lowness of a sound (स्वर की ऊँचाई-नीचाई, तारत्व)

The singer could not reach the high pitch of the final note → the note was too high to sing. This is the sound meaning.

Why the others are wrong.

• covered the pitch: the playing area of a cricket ground (पिच, खेल की पट्टी).

• pitch our tents: to set up (तंबू गाड़ना).

• a confident pitch to the investors: a sales talk or proposal (प्रस्ताव, प्रस्तुति).

Answer: The singer could not reach the high pitch of the final note.

One spelling, four jobs: ground, set up, sales talk, sound. Look for the music clue (singer, note).

option_1.en: A reservoir cut to store the town's drinking water

option_2.en: A tidal dockyard for berthing and floating out boats

option_3.en: A ritual tank used for ceremonial bathing by priests

option_4.en: A sump that carried the city's waste water away

question.en: What does the brick-lined basin with an inlet channel and spill-way at Lothal demonstrate?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 2 — A tidal dockyard for berthing and floating out boats

Lothal, on the Bhogavo in Gujarat, has a baked-brick basin over 200 metres long on its eastern side, fitted with an inlet channel and a spill-way that held water back at high tide — the feature on which its identification as a dockyard rests.

The mud-brick platform beside it is read as a warehouse, and the bead factory and the Persian Gulf seal found here support Lothal's role in overseas trade.

A reservoir, a ritual tank and a drain are all real Harappan structures, but at Dholavira, Mohenjo-daro and in the street drainage respectively.

Revision note — Lothal and the Harappan ports

  • Lothal lies in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat, on the Bhogavo, a tributary of the Sabarmati; it was excavated by S. R. Rao from 1955.
  • Finds at Lothal: a bead-making factory, a Persian Gulf seal, a terracotta model of a ship, rice husk, fire altars and a double burial.
  • Carnelian beads from Lothal and Chanhudaro reached Mesopotamia, where Harappan goods were called Meluhha.
  • Other coastal or trading sites: Sutkagendor and Balakot on the Makran coast, Allahdino, Kuntasi and Dholavira on Khadir island in Kutch.
  • The Great Bath is at Mohenjo-daro; the granary at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro; the ploughed field at Kalibangan.
  • Chanhudaro is the only major Harappan city with no citadel, and was a bead and seal making centre.
  • Dholavira is known for its three-part town plan, its water reservoirs and the ten-sign signboard.
  • Harappan seals were made of steatite, usually square, and most carry the unicorn motif.

option_1.en: The Golgi apparatus digests worn-out organelles and is called the cell's suicide bag

option_2.en: Lysosomes hold their hydrolytic enzymes at an acidic pH inside a single membrane

option_3.en: The Golgi apparatus packages secretory material and buds off lysosomes from its edges

option_4.en: The large central vacuole of a plant cell stores sap and maintains its turgidity

question.en: Which one of the following statements about cell organelles is NOT correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 1 — The Golgi apparatus digests worn-out organelles and is called the cell's suicide bag

It is the lysosome that is called the suicide bag: it carries some 40 hydrolytic enzymes — proteases, lipases and nucleases — that work best at an acidic pH of about 5, and on rupture they digest the cell itself.

The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages material coming from the endoplasmic reticulum and gives rise to lysosomes; the two work in sequence, but only one of them is the digestive bag.

Revision note — Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and vacuoles

  • The Golgi apparatus, described by Camillo Golgi in 1898, is a stack of flattened cisternae with a cis (forming) face and a trans (maturing) face; in plants it is called the dictyosome.
  • It forms lysosomes, secretory vesicles and the cell plate of a dividing plant cell.
  • Lysosomes were discovered and named by Christian de Duve, a Nobel laureate of 1974.
  • Lysosomal enzymes are made on the rough endoplasmic reticulum and packed by the Golgi.
  • Lysosomes carry out intracellular digestion, autophagy and the breakdown of worn-out organelles.
  • A plant vacuole is bounded by the tonoplast and can take up to 90% of the cell's volume.
  • Contractile vacuoles throw out excess water in Amoeba and Paramecium; food vacuoles digest ingested food.
  • Only mitochondria and plastids carry their own DNA and ribosomes; ribosomes themselves have no membrane.

question.en:
Consider the following statements about NASSCOM.

I. Rajesh Nambiar is its President.

II. He took over the post from Debjani Ghosh.

III. It is a statutory body set up by an Act of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 4 — I and II only

Rajesh Nambiar, formerly Chairman and Managing Director of Cognizant India, is the President of NASSCOM, having taken charge from Debjani Ghosh, who led the body from 2018.

NASSCOM is not statutory: it is a not-for-profit industry association of the technology sector, set up in 1988 and headquartered at Noida. Its Chairperson is an industry leader who serves for a year, while the President is the full-time executive head.

Revision note — industry bodies and who heads them

  • NASSCOM — National Association of Software and Service Companies; founded 1988; headquarters Noida; President Rajesh Nambiar.
  • CII (Confederation of Indian Industry) — traces its origin to 1895; headquarters New Delhi; Director General Chandrajit Banerjee; its President changes every financial year.
  • FICCI — set up in 1927 by G. D. Birla and Purshottamdas Thakurdas; headquarters New Delhi.
  • ASSOCHAM — Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India, founded in 1920.
  • These four are industry associations; the statutory regulators in their fields are bodies such as SEBI, the RBI and TRAI.
  • NITI Aayog, by contrast, is neither constitutional nor statutory — an executive think tank created on 1 January 2015 with the Prime Minister as Chairperson.
  • Other heads to revise: V. Narayanan (Chairman, ISRO, January 2025), Arvind Panagariya (16th Finance Commission), Ravneet Kaur (Competition Commission of India).
  • C. S. Setty chairs the State Bank of India; Vijaya Kishore Rahatkar heads the National Commission for Women.

question.en:
Match List-I with List-II, using the figures announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.

List-I (Figure)

List-II (Indicator)

A. 4.3% of GDP

1. Effective capital expenditure

B. 55.6%

2. Nominal GDP growth

C. 17.1 lakh crore rupees

3. Fiscal deficit

D. 10%

4. Debt-to-GDP ratio

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 3 — A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2

The Union Budget 2026-27 puts the fiscal deficit at 4.3% of GDP and the debt-to-GDP ratio at 55.6%, against a stated aim of bringing debt down to about 50% by 2030-31.

Capital expenditure is 12.2 lakh crore rupees, while effective capital expenditure — capex plus grants to states for creating capital assets — is 17.1 lakh crore rupees. Growth is assumed at 10% nominal and about 7% real.

Revision note — Union Budget 2026-27

  • The Budget is the Annual Financial Statement under Article 112; the word 'Budget' itself does not appear in the Constitution.
  • It is prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance.
  • Headline numbers: fiscal deficit 4.3%, debt-GDP 55.6%, capex 12.2 lakh crore rupees, effective capex 17.1 lakh crore rupees.
  • The new Income Tax Act 2025 takes effect from 1 April 2026, with no change in slabs — nil up to 4 lakh rupees, rising to 30% above 24 lakh rupees.
  • Securities Transaction Tax on options raised from 0.1% to 0.15% and on futures from 0.02% to 0.05%; TCS reduced to 2%.
  • The Electronics Manufacturing Scheme outlay was raised to 40,000 crore rupees, and Biopharma SHAKTI gets 10,000 crore rupees over five years.
  • An interim Budget has no constitutional basis; what Parliament passes with it is a vote-on-account.
  • A vote-on-account covers only expenditure; the full Budget must be passed before the money can be spent for the year.

Term

What it measures

Fiscal deficit

Total expenditure minus total receipts other than borrowings

Revenue deficit

Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts

Primary deficit

Fiscal deficit minus interest payments

Effective capital expenditure

Capex plus grants-in-aid to states for capital assets

Do not mix these up

  • Capital expenditure and effective capital expenditure are different lines — the second adds grants given to states to build assets.

Also asked from this topic: the IMF's projection for India's GDP growth (SSC GD 2026), the FDI India attracted between 2014 and 2025 (SSC MTS 2025), and the RBI's revised GDP growth projection for FY 2025-26 (RRB NTPC UG CBT-1 2025-26).

question.en:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index.

I. A state scores better if its revenue expenditure to capital outlay ratio rises.

II. A fall in its interest payment to revenue receipts ratio improves a state's score.

III. It is a composite of five parameters drawn from CAG data.

Which of the above statements are correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 2 — II and III only

The index rewards capital spending, so a higher revenue expenditure to capital outlay ratio — more money going on salaries, pensions and interest than on assets — pulls a state's score down. Statement I therefore reads the parameter backwards.

A smaller interest payment to revenue receipts ratio means a lighter debt-servicing burden and a better score, and the index is a composite of five parameters computed from CAG accounts.

Revision note — Fiscal Health Index

  • Published by NITI Aayog; the first edition was released in January 2025, using CAG data for FY 2022-23 and covering 18 major states.
  • Its five sub-indices are Quality of Expenditure, Revenue Mobilisation, Fiscal Prudence, Debt Index and Debt Sustainability. Each is built from fiscal indicators; these are not simply five individual ratios.
  • Odisha topped the first edition, followed by Chhattisgarh, Goa, Jharkhand and Gujarat.
  • In the second edition, released in 2026, the top performers are Odisha, Goa and Jharkhand.
  • Bihar moved up from Aspirational to Performer, while Tamil Nadu slipped down the rankings but stayed a Performer.
  • The bottom (Aspirational) group is West Bengal, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Punjab.
  • States account for about two-thirds of public spending and one-third of total revenue, which is why the index exists.
  • NITI Aayog's other indices: SDG India Index, Export Preparedness Index, India Innovation Index, Composite Water Management Index and the National Multidimensional Poverty Index.
